+prefix and print `wb.sheetnames` before concluding the sheet is missing.
+**A single cell such as `C14` is a range of one cell, and enumerating it needs care.**
+`ws["C14"]` returns a bare `Cell`, while `ws["C14:C14"]` and `ws["C3:C6"]` return a tuple of
+row tuples — so the usual idiom
+```python
+for row in ws[rng]:              # raises TypeError: 'Cell' object is not iterable
+    for cell in row:             # whenever rng names exactly one cell
+        print(cell.coordinate)
+fails on every single-cell `answer_position`. Enumerate coordinates from the range bounds
+instead, which works for one cell and for a rectangle alike:
+```python
+from openpyxl.utils import range_boundaries, get_column_letter
+c1, r1, c2, r2 = range_boundaries("C14")          # -> (3, 14, 3, 14)
+cells = [get_column_letter(c) + str(r)
+         for r in range(r1, r2 + 1) for c in range(c1, c2 + 1)]
+Use this form in every round — the inspection round as well as the verification round.
